events.summary: Solid first cut with good sourcing from ANPSA, iNaturalist/Wikipedia, Australian National Arboretum, and multiple horticultural references. The toxicity picture is nuanced — the tree itself is generally considered non-toxic to people and pets, but seed-pod hairs are a genuine irritant and that is the real hazard to communicate. Invasive status for B. rupestris specifically in Florida could not be confirmed from authoritative FISC/FLEPPC sources; the Dave's Garden FLEPPC Category II flag almost certainly refers to the related B. populneus, not B. rupestris.
